chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Five [conditions] are released [from the restriction of waiting period] in every state: the pregnant woman, the one who has despaired of menstruation, the one with whom he has not had sexual intercourse, the one whose husband is absent, and the one who has not attained puberty.
ai.seo_question: What are the five conditions under which a woman can be divorced immediately in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the five specific states in which a husband may divorce his wife immediately, bypassing the standard prohibition against divorcing a menstruating woman. This ruling highlights the juristic distinction between the physical state of menstruation and other biological or situational conditions such as pregnancy, menopause, pre-consummation, husband's absence, and pre-puberty, ensuring the waiting period (iddah) is calculated correctly in each unique scenario.
